claim: The CloudFront managed prefix list contains the IP address ranges of all CloudFront origin-facing servers. If your origin is on AWS and protected by a VPC security group, you can use the prefix list to allow inbound traffic to the origin only from CloudFront origin-facing servers, which prevents non-CloudFront traffic from reaching it; CloudFront maintains the list so that it stays up to date.

evidence.quote: The CloudFront managed prefix list contains the IP address ranges of all of the CloudFront globally distributed origin-facing servers.
The prefix list allows inbound traffic to your origin only from CloudFront origin-facing servers, which prevents non-CloudFront traffic from reaching your origin.

If your origin is hosted on AWS and protected by an Amazon VPC [security group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-security-groups.html), you can use the CloudFront managed prefix list.
CloudFront maintains the managed prefix list so it's always up to date with the IP addresses of all of the CloudFront global origin-facing servers.
